partners.mechanism_chain: NPHP1 (HGNC:8001) —DISRUPTS→ nephron development (GO:0001657); nephron development (GO:0001657) —LEADS_TO→ Kidney hypoplasia (HP:0000077); TMEM67 (HGNC:29657) —DISRUPTS→ cilium assembly and function (GO:0008103); cilium assembly and function (GO:0008103) —LEADS_TO→ Cerebellar vermis hypoplasia (HP:0001271); cilium assembly and function (GO:0008103) —LEADS_TO→ Retinal degeneration (HP:0000547). Loss-of-function mutations in NPHP1 disrupt nephron development, leading to kidney hypoplasia (Joubert syndrome 6). Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in TMEM67 disrupt cilium assembly and function, contributing to phenotypes like cerebellar vermis hypoplasia and retinal degeneration (Senior-Loken syndrome 1). The convergence is on the shared biological processes of kidney development and ciliary function, which are critical for both normal renal and neurological/visual development.

#### 1. Senior-Loken syndrome 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.450)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5620912)

**Proposed mechanism:** NPHP1 (HGNC:8001) —DISRUPTS→ nephron development (GO:0001657); nephron development (GO:0001657) —LEADS_TO→ Kidney hypoplasia (HP:0000077); TMEM67 (HGNC:29657) —DISRUPTS→ cilium assembly and function (GO:0008103); cilium assembly and function (GO:0008103) —LEADS_TO→ Cerebellar vermis hypoplasia (HP:0001271); cilium assembly and function (GO:0008103) —LEADS_TO→ Retinal degeneration (HP:0000547). Loss-of-function mutations in NPHP1 disrupt nephron development, leading to kidney hypoplasia (Joubert syndrome 6). Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in TMEM67 disrupt cilium assembly and function, contributing to phenotypes like cerebellar vermis hypoplasia and retinal degeneration (Senior-Loken syndrome 1). The convergence is on the shared biological processes of kidney development and ciliary function, which are critical for both normal renal and neurological/visual development.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in NPHP1 exclusively affect kidney development without impacting ciliary function, or that TMEM67 mutations do not affect kidney development, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Identification of a common pathogenic variant (AF > 0.1%) in NPHP1 or TMEM67 in the general population.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathways disrupted in Joubert syndrome 6 and Senior-Loken syndrome 1 could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting common downstream effectors or pathways, potentially benefiting patients with either condition. For example, therapies aimed at improving ciliary function or supporting nephron development could be explored.
